Given how large TVs are these days, it seems pretty obvious that higher resolutions in consoles is desirable. In PC games this would seem like less of an issue.

Depends. The minimum resolution a game needs is not based on any set standard. It should be each game needs enough resolution to get the job done.

For example:

Towerfall: Ascension. 8 bit graphics work just fine. You can up the resolution but it won't make the game any better. What you are meant to do in the game can be accomplished just fine at 8bit.

Contrast with Skyrim.

The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim. Imagine playing that at 8 bit resolution. It would not just be ugly looking but you would have a hard time performing the actions you are meant to do. Can't read books, or subtitles. Difficult to aim a bow. Is that a giant ahead or just a rock?

I think the focus on higher graphics has diverted to many resources away from development of fun games. There's plenty of games out there that look gorgeous but are terrible to play.
